claim: Resistance and regret are the two dreaded R words
Resistance is part of our life and always will be
When we don't fight resistance, we end up with the pain of regret, which is absolute poison
Number one with regret: let go of the past
Too many of us hang on to past failures and screw ups until they become sort of part of our identity
We can't do anything about the past, good or bad, not even relive the good stuff: work on living life today
The key thing with regret: what will you regret in the future?
We're all going to die
Imagine repeating the major parts of today, or of the average day last week, for the next 70 years: would you be happy, or have regrets?
The things you'd regret repeating for the next 70 years are the things to change, the ones we have control over
We often have goals, getting in shape, a better job, a business, a relationship, and sometimes they seem too big because we mentally try to do the whole thing at once, overnight
Reaching goals doesn't happen at once, overnight: stuff takes time, a reality we can accept or not

Accepting that stuff takes time, we benefit from a major fact: as soon as you take one step toward what you want to change, improve or add, even the tiniest, you've instantly punched resistance in the face, destroyed that regret and shifted your energy
Imagine dying a week from now after an accident, on a hospital bed, as your life kind of flashes before you: maybe some awesome memories, and regret for what you didn't do
If you talk to older people around you, and as we all experience once we get some age behind us, we realize the things we don't do are the ones we'll really regret
Just do what you'd regret not doing: after one step, at least you tried
The empowering thing: we don't have to accomplish huge changes before we start avoiding regret and getting sort of some energy transfer toward the goal
Avoiding regret and getting sort of some energy transfer toward the goal starts the moment you take some kind of action
Doing a big change all at once is impossible, so the task seems impossible
Dial a big change back: one little step to shift the energy, then one more. That's the way changes happen
Haven't worked out in three weeks? Set a timer for 1 minute and do something for 1 minute: you got a workout in today that you didn't get in yesterday
One little step for a business: what activity do you need to do every day to build it? If days have gone by with zero minutes of it, do 5 minutes
One little step for a relationship to repair, with your spouse or whoever: talk for a couple minutes, say something a little uncomfortable, open up a little more
Where we feel stuck, that's resistance kicking our ass
The best way to gain ground back from resistance is a little action: standing back up after he's been pounding on you and giving him a little jab to the face. That shifts things entirely

So far from perfect: so many years letting resistance win in so many ways, ground gained in some, still working on it. Life is a journey for all of us, and we can all start with one little bit of extra action
If something you'd regret not doing has been eating at you, start by writing it down: get it into the physical world, even if you throw the paper away
Even better than just writing down something you'd regret not doing, make it a goal and read it every day: that kind of repetition is really powerful to dial things into our mind
Even if you do nothing with it, ever, writing down the change you'd regret not making shifts the energy a little
After writing down a change you'd regret not making, if it's a workout thing, do that one-minute workout tomorrow, or tonight before bed
Probably too many of us live with too much regret all the time for what we're not doing, already feeling some of what will be really painful at the end of life
Weeks go by while something eats at you and you take no action: it feels shitty, we feel stuck and regret day to day
The day-to-day regret of weeks going by with no action is a fraction of the regret at the end of life if we didn't at least try
Whatever change you need to avoid regret: a better job, switching industries, a business
If your relationship sucks, commit to fixing it, or if it can't be fixed, move on
If you've neglected being as much of a father as you could be because you've been working, take one little step, and you can instantly shift away from that regret
This weekend, with the little extra time we probably mostly have, take a little action on something you've been stuck on: one minute, 30 seconds, five minutes
Right after this episode, write down the change you've been stuck on, do push-ups for a minute, or write out how you'll change your diet
You're stronger than you think you are
